answer.explanation: The portfolio starts at $100,000. Following a $12,000 deposit, the total portfolio value becomes $112,000 with $14,000 in cash. The target allocations are 60% STOCK ($67,200), 30% BOND ($33,600), and 10% CASH ($11,200). Since AAPL cannot be sold, its 100 shares remain ($22,000), which represents 19.64% of the final portfolio (well below the 25% maximum individual stock limit). To reach the target allocations using whole shares, we sell 25 shares of MSFT (raising $10,000), buy 41 shares of VOO (costing $20,500), and buy 110 shares of BND (costing $8,800). This exhausts the available cash, leaving a final cash balance of $0 (0.00% allocation, within the 0.5% tolerance of the 10% target). Final asset allocations achieve STOCK at 60.09%, BOND at 30.00%, and CASH at 9.91%, all within the permitted ±0.5 percentage point tolerance.
